categories.main_business_segments: Cardinal Health operates through two main business segments: Pharmaceutical and Medical. The Pharmaceutical segment distributes branded and generic pharmaceuticals, specialty pharmaceuticals, and over-the-counter healthcare products, and provides related services in the U.S. The Medical segment manufactures, sources, and distributes Cardinal Health-branded and national brand medical, surgical, and laboratory products, and provides supply chain services to healthcare providers globally.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced distribution logistics, inventory management systems, and automated technology platforms (such as Wavemark) for inventory management. In manufacturing, Cardinal Health uses both in-house production and sourcing from third parties for medical products, with a focus on quality systems, regulatory compliance, and supply chain efficiency. The company also operates nuclear pharmacies and radiopharmaceutical manufacturing facilities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cardinal Health serves hospitals, healthcare systems, pharmacies (including retail chains and independents), ambulatory surgery centers, clinical laboratories, physician offices, and patients in the home. Its largest customers are CVS Health and OptumRx, which together accounted for 41% of fiscal 2022 revenue. The company also works with group purchasing organizations (GPOs) and specialty pharmaceutical providers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s primary operations are in the United States, but it also has significant activities in Canada, Europe, Asia, and other international markets. The Medical segment operates manufacturing facilities in multiple countries, including Canada, Germany, Ireland, Japan, Malaysia, Malta, Mexico, and Thailand.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cardinal Health primarily operates as a midstream distributor in the healthcare supply chain, connecting manufacturers with healthcare providers and end users. In the Medical segment, it also has upstream activities through manufacturing and downstream activities through direct-to-home distribution.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include enhancing supply chain efficiency, expanding Cardinal Health-branded product offerings, investing in information technology infrastructure, and evolving commercial contracting for greater pricing flexibility. The company is focused on mitigating inflationary and supply chain pressures, pursuing selective acquisitions, and driving innovation in specialty pharmaceuticals and inventory management solutions.
categories.revenue_model: Cardinal Health generates revenue primarily through the sale and distribution of pharmaceuticals and medical products. Additional revenue streams include supply chain services, pharmacy management, consulting, and patient support services. The company also receives fees from distribution services agreements and sourcing ventures.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In pharmaceuticals, Cardinal Health competes with McKesson and AmerisourceBergen, as well as regional distributors and specialty providers. In medical products, competitors include Medline, Owens & Minor, and Becton, Dickinson and Company. Cardinal Health is one of the three largest pharmaceutical distributors in the U.S. and a major player in medical products distribution.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2022, Cardinal Health reported $181.4 billion in revenue, representing a 12% increase from the prior year. The company had a GAAP operating loss of $596 million due to a $2.1 billion goodwill impairment in the Medical segment, but non-GAAP operating earnings were $1.99 billion. The company maintains significant scale, with approximately 46,500 employees and a global footprint, but faces margin pressures and litigation-related costs.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cardinal Health emphasizes supply chain efficiency, broad product selection, and integrated solutions that connect manufacturers, providers, and patients. Its value proposition includes customized solutions, cost-effective distribution, proprietary branded products, and technology-enabled inventory management, aiming to improve patient care and reduce healthcare costs for its customers.
